jobs.title: Senior Director, Reporting & Analytics Engineering
jobs.description_text: Role Overview: We are seeking a Senior Director to lead our Enterprise Reporting and Analytics Engineering organization, a team of analytics engineers, report developers, visualization specialists, and people leaders. This organization focuses on the last mile of the enterprise data supply chain: the semantic models, curated data products, metric definitions, and consumption experiences that turn engineered data into decisions. This is not a traditional reporting leadership role; the classic notion of “reporting” in the form of a myriad of dashboards and filters is racing towards obsolescence. But the need for data and insights, and the need to deliver it in a way that is digestible and actionable, is timeless. Yes, governed dashboards and trusted reporting remain the foundation, and this leader must be excellent at that foundation. But the mandate is to move the organization decisively beyond static reporting toward a proactive, intelligent analytics capability: partnering with Data Science to productize and visualize their models, enabling generative AI and LLM-based access to our data, building exception-based systems that alert users when outcomes deviate from expectation in a statistically meaningful way, and designing agents that monitor data continuously and deliver insight without being asked. jobs.title: Research Intern, Frontier Agents (Summer 2027)
jobs.description_text: About the Role The Agents team investigates how to build, align, and scale frontier AI systems that can tackle complex, multi-step tasks and workflows across text and speech, with a particular focus on agentic and scientific domains. Our work sits at the intersection of agent capabilities, human-computer interaction, and infrastructure—from designing post-training methods for agentic behavior to developing evaluation frameworks for open-ended tasks where traditional metrics fall short. As a research intern, you will work on problems at the frontier of agentic AI, where challenges in alignment, reliability, and scalability are deeply intertwined. Projects may involve developing new training recipes for self-learning and long-horizon reasoning, curating datasets for non-deterministic scientific and agentic tasks, studying failure modes in agentic behavior, or building infrastructure that enables agent operations at scale. You'll operate in a space where algorithmic innovation, dataset and interaction design, and systems work come together to push the boundaries of what AI agents can reliably accomplish. jobs.title: Research Intern, Frontier Speculative Decoding (Summer 2027)
jobs.description_text: About the Role The Speculative Decoding team at Together AI builds the draft models and algorithms that let large language models generate faster without changing their outputs. Our speculators run in production on frontier open models such as DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM. Our work sits at the intersection of model training, inference algorithms and serving systems, and we co-design all three to lower the cost and latency of generation. As a research intern, you will dive into open questions in speculative decoding: new drafter architectures and verification schemes, knowledge distillation and training recipes that align draft and target models, and drafters that adapt as traffic shifts. You will train and fine-tune draft models at scale on dedicated GPU clusters, and test your ideas against realistic serving workloads, including long-context and agentic traffic. Projects aim to answer important research questions in speculative decoding, enabling faster generation on frontier models, drafters that keep pace with changing workloads, and robust, reproducible evaluation under real traffic. jobs.title: (Senior/Junior AI Inference Reliability Engineer, Compute Infra
jobs.description_text: About this role We're looking for a software engineer, reliability-minded but still a builder, to own what happens in production to the Kubernetes-native control plane that provisions and runs our GPU inference fleet. The platform team builds the manifest-driven API and controllers that let the inference team declare what they need, a cluster, a model deployment, a capacity change, and get it reconciled underneath. Your job is to keep that promise true in the real world: triaging InfiniBand issues when prefill and decode nodes stall exchanging KV cache over RDMA, diagnosing hero-model and LoRA-serving faults that don't show up in generic health checks, and extending the automated self-healing system so each new failure mode becomes a permanent fix instead of a recurring page. The core value we're after is keeping the decoupling real even when things break, and keeping the fleet efficient without that efficiency becoming a new source of instability. You'll own SLOs and error budgets for inference serving, lead incident response, and turn what postmortems teach you into actual changes in the controllers and automation, not just updated runbooks. You'll also work the reliability side of capacity efficiency, since a mistuned defragmentation or bin-packing pass is itself a production risk. Strong candidates have hands-on production-reliability experience on large-scale distributed or GPU-serving systems, are comfortable troubleshooting InfiniBand/RDMA and Kubernetes controller/CRD

jobs.title: Technical Writer Intern, Developer Experience (Summer 2027)
jobs.description_text: About the Developer Experience team The Developer Experience (DevX) team owns how developers learn and build on Together AI. We treat docs as a product and as code. Content lives in Git, publishes through Mintlify, and stays in sync with the API through CI/CD automation built on GitHub Actions. We also write for two audiences at once: the human developer reading a guide, and the AI coding agent pulling our docs into its context window. That means a house style guide built for AI-assisted authoring, structured content agents can parse, and automated review passes that check drafts against our quality bar. Role Overview As a Technical Writer Intern on DevX, you will write, test, and ship documentation that thousands of developers use to build with open-weight models. jobs.description_text: À propos de l’entreprise À Torc, nous avons toujours cru que la technologie des véhicules autonomes transformera la façon dont nous voyageons, transportons la marchandise et faisons des affaires. Leader de la conduite autonome depuis 2007, Torc a passé plus d’une décennie à commercialiser des solutions aux côtés de partenaires chevronnés. Nous faisons maintenant partie de la famille Daimler, ce qui nous permet de nous concentrer uniquement sur le développement de logiciels pour les camions automatisés. Nous transformerons la façon dont le monde transporte la marchandise. Joignez-vous à notre équipe : catapultez votre carrière au sein de l’entreprise ayant contribué à créer la technologie de conduite autonome (CA). Nous sommes la première entreprise de logiciels de CA ayant eu la vision de faire équipe directement avec un constructeur de camions. À propos du poste Nous sommes à la recherche d’annotateurs(trices) de données minutieux(ses) pour se joindre à notre équipe dans le cadre d’un poste à durée déterminée de six mois. Une prolongation ou une conversion en emploi régulier pourra être envisagée selon les besoins de l’entreprise et le rendement, mais n’est pas garantie. Dans ce rôle, vous contribuerez au processus d’annotation et d’assurance qualité des données de Torc en étiquetant des informations provenant de différents capteurs, notamment des images et des données LiDAR, afin d’aider à entraîner les systèmes d’intelligence artificielle utilisés dans les camions autonome

jobs.title: Senior, ML Engineer - Tracking
jobs.description_text: Meet the Team Accurate and highly available information about other actors and objects is fundamental to the safe operation of autonomous trucks. Core capabilities depend on accurate tracking estimates to ensure safe and efficient vehicle behavior. The Tracking Team develops the ML models, state estimation algorithms, and production software responsible for associating and estimating the kinematics of other actors and objects in real time. Our solutions fuse information from multiple sensors and maintain robust performance despite sensor imperfections, environmental challenges, and system degradation. As part of this team, you will develop and deploy production-ready tracking solutions and help solve the challenges of bringing autonomous vehicle technology to real-world commercial applications. What You'll Do Design, develop, and deploy production ML models for multi-object tracking, including association, learned pose and kinematic estimation, and sensor fusion using camera, LiDAR, radar, and other vehicle sensors. Develop scalable training and evaluation workflows using PyTorch, distributed training infrastructure, and large-scale real-world datasets. Design and improve tracking and sensor fusion algorithms for robust vehicle pose and kinematics Analyze large-scale vehicle data to characterize performance, identify failure modes, and drive model and system improvements. Develop robust, efficient production software in modern C++ and Python across the full development lifecy
